methods.steps: Save the drawing and choose Plain SVG as the type; save a separate copy.
methods.limits: The manual describes Plain SVG as for sharing a drawing with people who might not use Inkscape.
Optimization options are typically lossless but can be tweaked for more aggressive cleaning.
SVGO has a plugin architecture; configuration comes from svgo.config.mjs or the --config option.
The output format is guessed from the file extension for output files.

methods.steps: Select the range; Home > Copy > Copy as Picture; in GIMP choose Edit > Paste as > Paste as New Image; then File > Export As and save as JPEG.
methods.limits: The result is a picture of the cells, not an editable workbook.

methods.steps: In Calc choose File > Export As > Export as PDF; open the PDF in GIMP and pick the page in the import dialog; then File > Export As and save as JPEG.
methods.limits: The PDF page layout decides what the image shows.

methods.steps: In Numbers choose File > Export To > PDF; open the PDF in Preview and choose File > Export, then JPEG in the Format pop-up.
Run ffmpeg -i tape-capture.avi -c:a mp2 -q:v 4 -c:v mpeg2video recording.mpg.
methods.limits: -c:v and -c:a select encoders; -q sets a fixed quality scale.

methods.steps: In Python, run Image.open("photo.bin"), then .convert("RGB"), then .save("photo.jpg").
methods.limits: Image.open opens and identifies the given image file; the save format is determined from the filename extension.
The command takes an input image and an output name whose extension picks the format.

methods.steps: File > Import; choose the BMP; select Embed in the dialog that asks to link or embed.
methods.limits: Embeds the picture; does not trace it.
The input should be black and white; -s selects the SVG backend and -o names the output.
-c copy selects stream copy, which copies the streams without encoding them again.

methods.steps: File > Export Video; leave the Default settings, which make an H.264 MP4; click Export File.
methods.limits: Encodes again with the export settings.

methods.steps: Open the GIF; File > Export As with an .avif name; adjust the options in the AVIF dialog.
methods.limits: The dialog offers Lossless, Quality, Pixel format, Bit depth, Encoder speed and metadata options.
The [0] suffix selects the first frame; the formats page lists AVIF as readable and writable.

methods.steps: Image.open the GIF; seek(0); save to a file ending in .avif.
methods.limits: The GIF loader supports seek and tell; AVIF is read and write; the save format comes from the extension.

methods.steps: Open the ICNS; optionally set the size property before load(); save an ICO with a sizes list.
methods.limits: Sizes larger than the original or above 256 are ignored.

methods.steps: Open the ICNS; File > Export As with an .ico name; choose sizes and the Compressed (PNG) option in the ICO dialog.
methods.limits: GIMP warns that not all programs can read compressed icons.
